replacements.instruction: Introduce Table 3 as the three-run document-quality summary for the four systems it displays, distinguishing benchmark-native from common-rubric evaluation and retaining the sample-SD scope before the paired-interval interpretation.
replacements.before: Table~\ref{tab:main-results} summarizes the pointwise results across the three benchmarks.
replacements.after: Table~\ref{tab:main-results} reports three-run mean document-quality scores with sample SDs for benchmark-native and common-rubric evaluation across the three benchmarks.

replacements.instruction: Scope the Table 3 ranking and paired-interval statement to the four displayed systems. Single-writer is an ablation/diagnostic rather than a prior-work baseline in Table 3, so do not fold its separate native-score behavior into this comparison paragraph.
replacements.before: \condAgenticCogWriter\ obtains the highest mean on every WritingBench and HelloBench measure, and its paired prompt-level differences exclude zero against every alternative on both WritingBench measures and on HelloBench native scores.
replacements.after: \condAgenticCogWriter\ obtains the highest displayed mean on every WritingBench and HelloBench measure, and its paired prompt-level differences exclude zero against every displayed alternative on both WritingBench measures and on HelloBench native scores.

replacements.instruction: Align the Discussion with Table 3's displayed-system scope and the paired DoLoMiTes evidence: Staged has the highest displayed DoLoMiTes pointwise mean, but its paired interval does not separate it from our system.
replacements.before: The system ranks first on WritingBench and HelloBench pointwise metrics but not DoLoMiTes, while pairwise evaluation favors it over single-pass generation, fixed writing stages, and adaptive task planning on every benchmark.
replacements.after: The system has the highest displayed means on WritingBench and HelloBench, whereas \condStaged has the highest DoLoMiTes pointwise mean without a paired interval separating it from our system; pairwise evaluation favors our system over single-pass generation, fixed writing stages, and adaptive task planning on every benchmark.
